Horokhiv Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Horokhiv, Ukraine

Demolished. This cemetery's founding is undocumented, though its earliest preserved tombstone dates to 1896, its latest to 1937; it was demolished, with gravestones repurposed for road construction, and Horokhiv's central market later built on the site. Gravestones remained visible near the cemetery until 1965, when local authorities removed them, some broken in half and used to pave roads. In April 2018, about 40 of these repurposed gravestones were rediscovered and relocated near the former cemetery site, where the local Jewish community, with local authority support, built a memorial from the fragments - located 60 meters south of the original grounds at Students and Halana Streets. The memorial also includes a tziyun to Itzchak Drubitscher, built under the supervision of Yisrael Meir Gabay. Jews settled in Horokhiv in the 16th century, first documented 1536; population reached 752 by 1765 and 2,571 by 1897. The community suffered severely during the Khmelnytsky uprising; in 1700, the Volyn Province Committee of the (Jewish) Council met in Horokhiv. Notable rabbis included Rabbi Abba'le and Rabbi Raphael Meizlisch, author of Tosefot Shabbat. WWI brought suffering under wartime conditions and Petliura forces; interwar Zionist organizations (He-Halutz, Beitar) were active, with Olyka, Trisk, and Stolin-Karlin Hasidic trends influencing the community. Population reached 3,120 by 1937. Wehrmacht occupation from June 24, 1941 established a ghetto that October, concentrating Horokhiv and area Jews, liquidated September 8, 1942. A 1990 monument marks the site where 300 Jews were murdered in August 1941.
